newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian-Chechen dialogue under new pressure.
newsitem.headline: Russian-Chechen dialogue under new pressure.

text.p: A meeting aimed at paving the way for talks between Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Chechen leader Aslan Maskhadov was postponed on Wednesday as tensions rose between Moscow and the separatist region.
A spokesman for Russia's powerful Security Council told Reuters the meeting between its secretary, Ivan Rybkin, and Chechen First Deputy Prime Minister Movladi Udugov had been put off.
"We need to coordinate a number of questions," said Sergei Sidorov without elaborating. He did not say when the meeting, originally set for Thursday, would now take place.

Sidorov denied the situation had worsened and said he did not think the decision to put off the meeting was directly linked to an incident earlier on Wednesday angily condemned by Udugov as "provocation".
Udugov said Russian fighter planes simulated an attack on the central market and airport in Grozny, the Chechen capital. Russia's military denied this.
Udugov, speaking to reporters in Grozny, accused "influential groupings" in Moscow of trying to sabotage the planned meeting between Yeltsin and Maskhadov.
"The aim of these provocative actions by Russian military aircraft is to undermine the trip of Maskhadov (to Moscow)," he said.
"The incident demonstrates that there are sufficiently influential groupings in Moscow that want a continuation of the conflict (between Russia and Chechnya)."

Udugov said he had filed a formal complaint with the Russian authorities, adding that officials in the Security Council had told him the planes came from a military training school at the southern town of Armavir.
Interfax news agency quoted a Russian airforce spokesman as saying no flights over Chechnya had taken place.

In a bizarre twist, sources in Chechnya's Interior Ministry earlier told Reuters the plane was actually Chechen and it had been rehearsing for a parade to mark the republic's Independence Day on September 6.
The sources mentioned only one plane while Udugov spoke about several aircraft.
Yeltsin reaffirmed his wish to meet Maskhadov in the near future but no date or venue was announced.

Russian news agencies quoted him as saying Moscow must fulfil all its obligations under agreements it signed with the region, including the release of funds to help to rebuild Chechnya's shattered economy and infrastructure.

"We have to fulfil what we promised," RIA Novosti news agency quoted Yeltsin as saying at a meeting in the Kremlin with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin. "Otherwise extremists (in Chechnya) criticise Maskhadov."
Kremlin sources had said the meeting was likely to take place on Friday or Saturday.

The latest row underlined the still widespread jitters in Chechnya about Russia's intentions a year after the two sides signed a peace pact ending a 21-month conflict in which tens of thousands of people were killed.
Talks aimed at normalising relations are stalled over the vexed issue of Chechnya's status, left unresolved when Russia withdrew its troops.
Maskhadov, buoyed by the separatists' battlefield victory, insists that his republic is fully independent but Yeltsin wants Chechnya to remain loosely within the Russian Federation.
